title: Graceful fallback for ephemeral prefix allocator to mitigate cross-tenant GPU OOMs and KV-index drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers (anonymized: Customer-A hosted, Customer-B dedicated) recently escalated sustained GPU OOMs correlated with rapid ephemeral session creation during bursty workloads. Root analysis shows the ephemeral prefix allocator can postpone reclaiming short-lived arena segments, leaving fragmented GPU slabs and stale KV-index entries. The combination caused allocation failures under realistic load patterns (short-run chat sessions + long-run embeddings). This ticket implements a conservative fallback path in the ephemeral prefix allocator and a lightweight KV-index janitor to prevent tombstone accumulation and restore allocatable slab continuity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a scaled tenant-sim workload with 2000 concurrent short-lived sessions (mean lifetime ~7s) and 50 long-running embedding streams
2) Configure hosted/dedicated node pool with default ephemeral allocator thresholds (thresholds v1.21), no forced compaction
3) Observe GPU memory fragmentation increase over 10-15 minutes and rising allocation failures leading to OOMs for new requests
4) Correlate with KV-index tombstone counts and session handle churn in logs
observed_symptoms: OOMs that occur without proportional total memory growth (fragmentation-driven)
KV-index tombstone growth when session handles churn rapidly
Slow tail latency increases before OOMs as allocation searches fail and retry
Customer-visible 5xx error spikes and degraded throughput for affected tenants
investigation_findings: Ephemeral prefix allocator defers coalescing in hot allocation paths to avoid CPU penalty — this leaves small unusable fragments on GPU slabs
KV-index tombstone reclamation was tuned for cold workloads; rapid churn leaves metadata behind causing allocation candidate lists to be larger and less contiguous
Cross-tenant eviction and coldstart heuristics didn't trigger early enough under burst patterns
Existing mitigations (short-term evictor backoff and tenant throttling) reduce impact but do not prevent recurrence at scale
proposed_solution: 1) Implement allocator graceful-fallback: when allocation search exceeds X attempts or fragmentation metric F > 0.45, run an aggressive local compaction for small arenas and enable immediate fallback to an alternate allocator path that reserves pre-coalesced slabs
2) Add a lightweight KV-index janitor background worker to sweep tombstones every Y seconds in high-churn tenants and reconsolidate index nodes to reduce scatter
3) Add tenant-scoped prewarm for hosted burst tokens to reduce cold allocation pressure on shared slabs
4) Instrument and expose fragmentation and tombstone-rate metrics in Console for per-tenant dashboards
5) Add canary rollout with step-down policy: enable fallback in 5% of nodes -> 25% -> 100% while monitoring OOM and tail latency
tradeoffs_and_risks: Aggressive compaction increases short CPU and kernel time per node; may slightly increase per-request latency for a small window
KV janitor increases background work and memory scanning cycles; must be rate-limited to avoid interfering with tight SLO customers
Fallback allocator complexity adds code paths; require thorough unit + integration tests to avoid regressions
Rollout needs tight monitoring to ensure we don't exacerbate latency for latency-sensitive customers
implementation_notes: Allocator change isolated under feature flag: runtime.ephemeral_allocator.fallback_enabled
KV janitor configurable: runtime.kv_janitor.interval_sec and runtime.kv_janitor.max_slab_bytes
New metrics emitted: allocator.fragmentation_ratio, kv.janitor_tombstones_reclaimed, tenant.prewarm_count
Unit tests: simulate high-churn allocation patterns and assert no memory leak; integration harness to run synthetic tenant churn on staging GPU nodes
PR will include a 'soft' mode that logs actions without performing compactions to validate heuristics
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge feature-flagged PR to canary branch; run synthetic churn test across CI-GPU matrix
Week 2: Canary rollout to 3% of hosted nodes and one dedicated cluster; enable soft-mode janitor
Week 3: Monitor metrics for 72 hours; iterate on thresholds (X and Y) with telemetry team
Week 4: Gradual rollout to 25% -> 75% -> 100% with scheduled maintenance windows for dedicated customers; provide rollback plan
Post-rollout: Run 7-day regression evals and collect customer feedback; include in runtime-1.22 release notes
monitoring_and_metrics: Primary: per-tenant GPU OOM count (oom.count), allocator.fragmentation_ratio (avg and p95), kv_index.tombstone_rate
Secondary: tail latency for generate/endpoints (p99), per-node CPU increase during compaction windows
Alerting: trigger P0 alert if OOMs increase > 3x baseline or fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 for >15 minutes
Dashboards: add tenant-level view in Console: fragmentation trend + reclaimed tombstones
mitigations_taken: Applied temporary tenant throttling and extended eviction timeout for Customer-A during investigation
Increased evictor aggressiveness for dedicated clusters as immediate fallback for Customer-B (manual change)
Provisioned additional spare GPU capacity in affected pods to reduce immediate customer impact
